solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Men disheartened with United become angry

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word for men is taken away

parts.note: gents is an informal word for men
having teamed up means having united, joined forces

explanation.surface: A football fan's temper rises as a joyless crowd of men watches Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes N, the central letter of GENTS, leaving GETS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: getting worked up like a boiling kettle is losing one's temper.

clue.text: Last bit in mug with some drinks

definitions.text: Last bit in mug with some drinks

indicators.note: the final letter of the word mug is taken

parts.note: rounds are sets of drinks bought for a group at the bar

explanation.surface: Describes the dregs left at the bottom of a cup after a drink or two.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the sediment is literally the last bit in a coffee mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee grounds are the residue that settles at the bottom of a cup once the liquid is drunk.

clue.text: See this weapon working, it might make you interested

indicators.note: when letters are working they are set in motion and rearranged, so the pool is shuffled

parts.note: the word whose letters make the pool, the answer's letters plus those of See
its three letters join the answer's letters in the shuffle

explanation.surface: An invitation to look at a weapon in action, promising it will grab your attention.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of SEE plus the answer, rearranged ('working'), make INTERESTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-pronged spear, as carried by Neptune, is a weapon; it is also a nuclear missile system.

clue.text: Note beer in bar calling to customers

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: one word goes in another, the beer placed inside the bar

parts.note: bar means except, less
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A musical note and a beer at the bar, as if a singer in a pub were calling to the drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is not a pub counter but a preposition meaning except, LESS; ALE goes into it to make LESALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Telephone selling is the business of ringing up potential buyers.

clue.text: He wrote article on model from the south

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom upwards turns the word backwards

parts.note: to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: An author pens an article about a model from the southern part of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' puts the second piece below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller is famous as the writer of the fables, so he is one who wrote.

clue.text: Fish sandwiches guy set over plates

indicators.note: the fish enclose the other piece like bread around a filling

parts.note: eels are fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, set over means turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: a guy is a man

explanation.surface: Someone serves fish sandwiches, a fellow arranging them over plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set over' turns the guy upside down, as a down clue reads upward; 'plates' is a verb, to coat metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to coat a metal surface with a thin protective or decorative layer.

clue.text: Restricting mobile apps, regularly barred upload somewhere in Scandinavia

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the shuffled ones within, confining them
every other letter is barred, so only the odd ones of upload survive
mobile means movable, so the letters of apps are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tech story: mobile apps restricted and uploads routinely blocked somewhere in the north of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly barred' keeps only the odd letters of upload, and the shuffled apps go in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A university city in Sweden, a Scandinavian country, so a place in that region.

clue.text: Description of trier? Not one likely to win

definitions.meaning: read cryptically, a rank (a tier) put on the outside of the letter R spells the word trier
a competitor given very long odds, a no-hoper

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as RANK OUTSIDE R: a rank is a tier, and TIER around R makes TRIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or competitor given very long odds is a no-hoper, unlikely to finish first.

clue.text: Area mined, coal is withdrawn

indicators.note: mined means dug up and broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A colliery area is worked out and its coal removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' looks like part of the mining scene, but it is the definition; 'mined' shuffles COAL IS into SOCIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shy and unsociable, avoiding the company of others, is retiring and reserved.

clue.text: One cuts bit of loaf well, but not the ends

parts.note: loaf is slang for head (from loaf of bread), and the scalp is part of it

indicators.note: the word well loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A baker's slicer cuts a piece of bread well but leaves the crusty ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' is rhyming slang: loaf of bread = head, whose skin is the scalp.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's small sharp knife is a tool that slices tissue.

clue.text: Bird World with no eagle, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lament that the world has lost its eagles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges WORLD and NO EAGLE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A species of owl with tall ear tufts, so a kind of bird.

clue.text: Boat's installed with tunnel in the middle for boarding place

indicators.note: the boat has the other letters fitted inside it

parts.note: keel is a poetic word for a boat, and the possessive adds S

indicators.note: only the central pair of letters of tunnel is taken

explanation.surface: A boat is fitted out with a tunnel through its middle so passengers can board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boarding' suggests getting on a boat, but it is where dogs are boarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs are lodged at these establishments while their owners are away, so they are boarding places.

clue.text: Give notice about contest in outskirts of Paignton

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the outer letters
the edges of the town name, its first and last letters

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a war is a contest

explanation.surface: Notice is given of a fight on the outskirts of a Devon seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Paignton is a seaside resort in Devon; only its outer letters P and N are used.
explanation.definitionFit: To alert in advance is to tell someone ahead of time, a form of giving notice.

clue.text: Tip from well-informed group

parts.note: to be up on something is to be well-informed about it
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A piece of advice passed on by people in the know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' reads as a piece of advice, but it is the verb meaning to overturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip something over is to knock it over, overturn it.

clue.text: Massage head after thumps and cover over shiner

indicators.note: the shuffled head comes after the blows

parts.note: to lamp someone is to hit them, so lamps means thumps

indicators.note: to massage is to knead, working the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A fighter's head is massaged after blows, and a cover is put over a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shiner' suggests a black eye, but here it is a lamp; 'Massage' shuffles HEAD into HADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade fits over a light bulb, and a lamp is something that shines.

clue.text: Like a go-between linking press and politician

parts.note: the press is the news media
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone acting as a go-between links journalists with a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A mediator acts between parties, so this adjective describes such a role.

clue.text: Brown starter of salmon not brought to the lips

indicators.note: the opening letter of salmon

parts.note: something never kissed has not been brought to the lips

explanation.surface: A fish starter is browned but nobody eats it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a cooking instruction, but it is the adjective meaning tanned.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin tanned by sunshine is bronzed, a golden or brown colour.

clue.text: Baby's very bright writing up letter in Greek

parts.note: neon describes glaringly bright fluorescent colour

indicators.note: in a down clue, written upwards means read backwards

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A child's dazzling writing contains a Greek letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Baby's' is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn infant less than about four weeks old, a very young child.

clue.text: One engineered solid base to put on a pedestal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: engineered means designed and constructed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word whose letters are shuffled
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: An engineer builds a firm base to mount something on a plinth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineered' turns SOLID into DOLIS; E is the mathematical constant used as the base of natural logs.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship or revere someone excessively is an idiom for elevating them above others.

clue.text: After assault, soldiers can't stand

indicators.note: the soldiers come after the assault

parts.note: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a UK criminal charge for a serious assault
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Troops are left exhausted after an attack, unable to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a British criminal offence; OR is the usual abbreviation for other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe or detest something is to find it intolerable.

clue.text: To manage account European invested in place of industry

indicators.note: invested means clothed or placed inside, so one letter goes into the other piece

parts.note: a hive is a busy place, as busy as bees

explanation.surface: Business jargon: managing an account means a European putting money into an industrial site.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed in doing something is to accomplish or bring it off.

clue.text: Obstinate policeman in hurry to be on time

indicators.note: the policeman goes inside the word for hurry

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, hurry
DS is a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: A stubborn officer rushes so as not to be late.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to be on' places T below the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly fixed and unwilling to change, stubborn in one's ways.

clue.text: Leave mock Tudor housing long-faced

indicators.note: the shuffled letters house the other piece, enclosing it
mock means imitation, so the letters of Tudor are rearranged

parts.note: po, short for po-faced, means solemn and humourless

explanation.surface: Someone glum quits a mock Tudor house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mock' rearranges TUDOR into DROUT; 'long-faced' is po-faced, cut short to PO.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit or withdraw from a course or society is to abandon it.

clue.text: Fortune to incorporate railway climbing mountainous region

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, backwards
one piece takes the other into its body

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: A fortune is spent on a mountain railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses the whole assembly, LRYOT, since a down answer reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alpine area of Austria and Italy, a region of high mountains.

clue.text: Stuck join, wrapping present

indicators.note: the outer word wraps around the other like paper round a gift

parts.note: to add is to join on
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Sticky tape is used to join wrapping paper around a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' suggests a gift but means here, not absent.
explanation.definitionFit: Clung or kept firmly attached, as glue keeps things together.

clue.text: One immersed in textbook is better prepared

indicators.note: one letter is plunged inside the other word

parts.note: a reader is a school textbook
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A student absorbed in study is better ready for the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative meaning more ready, more willing or set to go.

clue.text: Left, cut and ran

parts.note: over means left, remaining
to saw is to cut

explanation.surface: Three verbs of escape: someone left, cut off and ran away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran' suggests fleeing but means managed, as one runs a business.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise something is to manage it, as one runs a company.

clue.text: The German rejected job, shunning first motorway restructuring

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: der is the German masculine article for the

indicators.note: the opening letter is avoided, removed from the front of the word

parts.note: employment is a job
M is the abbreviation for a British motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A German turns down a job because it avoids the motorway, part of a reorganisation.
explanation.walkthrough: DER reversed gives RED; EMPLOYMENT loses its first letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving staff or forces to new positions is a reorganising of them.
